claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a coarse lamellar microstructure.
Solution treatment followed by controlled aging can nucleate fine, coherent precipitates within the eutectic lamellae.
Optimizing aging temperature and duration can prevent excessive precipitate coarsening.
The proposed treatment refines the microstructure through nanoscale coherent precipitation within the existing lamellar structure.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates increases strength.
The nanoscale precipitates promote localized strain accommodation.
Localized strain accommodation mitigates early fracture and thereby enhances ductility.
The treatment will produce a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will produce an appreciable increase in ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
Strength and ductility improvements require the precipitates to remain nanoscale and coherent.
Overaging or precipitate coarsening may reduce ductility or eliminate the anticipated strength gain.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that coarsened or incoherent precipitates fall outside the conditions under which improvement is expected, whereas the falsification rule treats observing coarsening or loss of coherence as itself falsifying the hypothesis.
